title: truncate_text can return more tokens than requested when only one non-marker token is available
reasoning: When the marker itself fits and leaves exactly one token of remaining budget, the code sets head to 1 and tail to 1, producing head + marker + tail and exceeding token_limit by one token. The fallback character estimator has the same shape when available is one character, so both paths can violate the caller's requested cap. This matters for prompt/window enforcement paths because a truncation helper that returns over-budget content can still overflow a strict context limit.
reproduction: Call TokenService.truncate_text with a long text, token_limit equal to len(marker_tokens) + 1, and a marker whose token count is smaller than token_limit. The returned litellm token sequence is tokens[:1] + marker_tokens + tokens[-1:], which is one token over budget.
recommendation: Allocate head and tail so their sum never exceeds available. For example, compute head = max(available // 2, 0), tail = available - head, and only force at least one side when available permits it. Mirror the same invariant in the fallback character truncation path.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were included for this feature, and the edge case requires a narrow token_limit where the marker leaves exactly one token of remaining budget.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a focused TokenService.truncate_text test that stubs litellm.encode/decode, uses token_limit = len(marker_tokens) + 1, and asserts the decoded truncated token list length is <= token_limit. Add the same edge case for the fallback path by forcing litellm.encode to raise.
minimumFixScope: backend/src/services/token_service.py truncation budget calculation plus focused backend tests for both litellm and fallback paths.
